avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Concurrent anticoagulants increase bleeding risk significantly
avoid_supplements.action: Do not combine with other anticoagulants unless directed by physician for bridging therapy

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 and CYP2C8 inducer reduces apixaban plasma concentrations and efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consult prescriber before use

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo Biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Antiplatelet and anticoagulant properties potentiate bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use only with close medical supervision and INR/bleeding monitoring

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic (High-dose supplements)
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose supplements; normal dietary garlic is acceptable

avoid_supplements.name: Cranberry Supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May inhibit CYP3A4 and CYP2C8, potentially increasing apixaban levels
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose cranberry supplements; discuss with provider

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (High-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet effect may additively increase bleeding risk
caution_supplements.action: Use standard dietary doses; monitor for unusual bleeding

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet properties; theoretical bleeding risk
caution_supplements.action: Use in culinary amounts; avoid high-dose supplements without monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin E (High-dose >400 IU)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Antiplatelet effect at high doses may increase bleeding risk
caution_supplements.action: Limit to dietary sources or standard supplementation; report any bleeding

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit Juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibitor significantly increases apixaban bioavailability and plasma concentrations, increasing bleeding risk
avoid_foods.action: Completely avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice during apixaban therapy

caution_foods.name: Cranberry Juice (High-volume consumption)
caution_foods.mechanism: May weakly inhibit CYP3A4; excessive intake could theoretically increase apixaban levels
caution_foods.action: Limit to occasional use; avoid daily high-volume consumption

caution_foods.name: Vitamin K-Rich Foods (Kale, Spinach, Broccoli)
caution_foods.mechanism: Unlike warfarin, apixaban is not vitamin K-dependent, but consistency in intake is preferable
caution_foods.action: Maintain consistent intake; no strict restriction needed

monitoring_notes: Apixaban has minimal food interactions compared to warfarin due to its predictable pharmacokinetics, but CYP3A4/2C8 inducers and inhibitors require caution. Monitor for signs of bleeding (bruising, blood in urine/stool, nosebleeds) and report concurrent medications or high-dose supplements to the prescribing provider, especially those affecting liver enzymes.
